original_question: Fix k >= 2 and assume m is sufficiently large. If G is F_{k,3}-free, where F_{k,3} = K_1 \/ kK_2 is the friendship graph made of k triangles sharing a common vertex, must lambda(G) be at most (k - 1 + sqrt(4m - k^2 + 1)) / 2, with equality only for K_k joined with an independent set of size m/k - (k - 1)/2?
target_in_paper: Section 3, friendship-graph subsection: Conjecture 3.28, read together with the Section 1 introductory notation and the nearby discussion of Theorem 3.38 and Conjectures 3.39–3.41.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the forbidden graph family F_{k,3} = K_1 ∨ kK_2, the fixed-parameter/large-size regime (fixed k, m sufficiently large), the intended upper bound λ(G) ≤ (k - 1 + √(4m - k^2 + 1))/2, and the intended extremal construction K_k ∨ ((m/k) - (k - 1)/2)K_1. That is the right friendship-graph conjecture recorded in the paper’s Section 3 as Conjecture 3.28.
missing_details: The paper’s ambient objects are simple finite undirected graphs; your draft leaves that implicit.
You should say explicitly that G has exactly m edges.
The paper’s notation λ(G) refers to the adjacency spectral radius of G; your draft assumes that without stating it.

The survey’s standard fixed-size class is 𝒢(m,F), the family of F-free graphs with m edges and no isolated vertices; even if isolated vertices do not affect λ(G), that paper-level setup is implicit in your draft.
For all sufficiently large m should be made explicit as: for each fixed integer k ≥ 2, there exists m0 = m0(k) such that the statement holds for all m ≥ m0.

The equality graph K_k ∨ ((m/k) - (k - 1)/2)K_1 only makes literal sense when s = (m - C(k,2))/k = (m/k) - (k - 1)/2 is a nonnegative integer; otherwise equality is impossible. Your draft leaves this integrality/congruence issue implicit.
To be fully stand-alone, the join notation ∨ and the notation sK_1 should be unpacked as the join of K_k with an independent set of size s.
To stay paper-faithful, it is helpful to signal that the nearby Section 3 discussion also treats other residue classes separately via Conjectures 3.39–3.41.
refined_question: For each fixed integer k ≥ 2, does there exist an integer m0 = m0(k) such that every simple finite undirected graph G with exactly m ≥ m0 edges that is F_{k,3}-free, where F_{k,3} = K_1 ∨ kK_2 is the friendship graph consisting of k triangles sharing a common vertex, satisfies λ(G) ≤ (k - 1 + √(4m - k^2 + 1))/2, where λ(G) is the adjacency spectral radius of G; and, moreover, is equality possible only when G is isomorphic to the join K_k ∨ sK_1 with s = (m - C(k,2))/k = (m/k) - (k - 1)/2 (so in particular s is a nonnegative integer)?
justification: The draft is targeting the paper’s friendship-graph conjecture, not a broader neighboring problem. In the survey’s Section 3, Conjecture 3.28 is the item about F_{k,3} = K_1 ∨ kK_2 and the extremal join graph K_k ∨ ((m/k) - (k - 1)/2)K_1. The Section 1 introduction supplies the meaning of λ(G) and the fixed-size notation 𝒢(m,F). The nearby Section 3 discussion of Theorem 3.38 and Conjectures 3.39–3.41 shows that congruence/integrality issues for the equality case are part of the immediate context, so the refined version makes that hidden condition explicit without broadening the scope beyond the survey’s actual intent.
